title: Is Microchip Technology Stock Underperforming the S&P 500?
excerpt: Microchip Technology has significantly underperformed the broader market over the past year, while analysts remain bullish on the company’s outlook.
content_html:
Microchip Technology Incorporated (MCHP) is a global semiconductor company focused on embedded control. The Chandler, Arizona-based company designs, manufactures, and sells microcontrollers, FPGAs, analog, power, connectivity, and timing components and systems for industrial, automotive, consumer, aerospace, defense, communications, and computing markets. The company has a market capitalization of approximately $40.3 billion.

Companies worth between $10 billion and $200 billion are generally classified as "large-cap stocks," and Microchip Technology comfortably fits this category. Its substantial market capitalization reflects its size, influence, and established presence in the semiconductor industry. Microchip benefits from a diverse portfolio of microcontrollers and analog chips serving consumer, automotive, and industrial markets. Its leadership in 8-bit MCUs, expansion into higher-end products, and opportunities in AI, IoT, automation, and connected devices support its long-term growth prospects.

Despite the notable feats, MCHP is currently 30% below its 52-week high of $105.91, reached on May 8, 2026. The stock has also declined 23% over the past three months, significantly underperforming the S&P 500 ($SPX), which has risen 1.8% over the same period.

The stock's 15.1% gain over the past 52 weeks has underperformed the S&P 500's 18.7% return over the same period. However, shares of MCHP have climbed 16.4% year-to-date, outperforming the SPX's 12.8% YTD gain. 

MCHP has traded below its 50-day moving average since late June and below its 200-day moving average since late August, suggesting a downward trend.

Microchip Technology lagged the broader market over the past year, potentially reflecting underlying weakness in its financial performance. Over the past five years, the company's revenue declined 2.1% annually, while EPS fell 9.6% and its free cash flow margin dropped 15 percentage points. These trends point to weaker demand and profitability pressures that may have weighed on investor sentiment.

However, MCHP shares jumped about 13.9% on August 7, after the company reported its fiscal Q1 2027 results. Its non-GAAP net income per share of 76 cents surpassed Wall Street's expectations of 70 cents, while net sales of $1.49 billion exceeded forecasts of $1.45 billion.
